title: Change Minimum Characters to Satisfy One of Three Conditions
summary: Given two strings a and b consisting of lowercase letters, you can change any character in a or b to any lowercase letter.
statement: Given two strings a and b consisting of lowercase letters, you can change any character in a or b to any lowercase letter. Your goal is to achieve one of the following conditions: 1. Every letter in a is strictly less than every letter in b in the alphabet. 2. Every letter in b is strictly less than every letter in a in the alphabet. 3. Both a and b consist of the same single letter. Return the minimum number of operations needed to satisfy any one of these conditions.
constraints: Minimize replacements so every a character is less than every b character, every b character is less than every a character, or both strings contain only one shared letter.
hints: The first two conditions are determined by one alphabet boundary; the third by one chosen letter.
Count letters, try all 25 boundaries in both directions, then all 26 shared letters.
For boundary c, replace a letters above c and b letters at or below c; reverse for condition two.
Every valid ordered pair has a boundary, and every one-letter result has a chosen letter, so the exhaustive 51 candidates include the optimum.
editorial: Every valid ordered pair has a boundary, and every one-letter result has a chosen letter, so the exhaustive 51 candidates include the optimum.

tests.explanation: Changing two letters can make every character in a smaller than every character in b.
The minimum across the two ordering directions and one-letter condition is three.
